newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippine copper output to hit all-time low in 97.
newsitem.headline: Philippine copper output to hit all-time low in 97.

text.p: Philippine copper output is seen slumping to an all-time low of 53,500 tonnes in 1997 from a peak in 1981 of 330,000 tonnes, the president of the Philippine Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR) said on Tuesday.

Alfredo San Miguel Junior said in a presentation at a copper conference in Singapore that Philippine copper production in 1996 reached only 62,297 tonnes. The Philippines used to be one of the 10 leading producers of copper in the world in 1981.
"The prospect for 1997 is even worse," he said.

With the copper mine of Atlas Consolidated Mining and Industrial Corp still closed and the continuing shutdown of Marcopper's mine on central Marinduque island after a waste spill, production will slide to its lowest level ever, San Miguel said.
"New mine projects are not likely to open up within five years time as most of the prospects are still in the exploration or feasibility stage," he said.

The approval of a mining law in 1995 which has allowed foreign mining companies up to a 100 percent control in a venture has led to massive interest in the exploration of mineral-rich areas of Luzon and Mindanao islands.
Promising projects on both islands are still "awaiting the completion of metallurgical and feasibility studies," he said.

"Mine projects in the Philippines, to be viable, will require by-product credits, especially gold, to enhance their ore values. Deposits discovered to date do not match the size of Indonesian, Peruvian or Chilean finds," he added.
But the PASAR president said copper demand in the Philippines should remain healthy .
"With the continued growth of the Philippine economy, the local market share would become increasingly important to PASAR," San Miguel said.
He quoted the Philippine Electric Wire Manufacturers Association as estimating that domestic copper consumption will expand to 105,000 tonnes in 2001 from 56,600 tonnes in 1996.
